**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 91, verses 9–15:**

**On the words of Allah, ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾ (91:9)**

He says: He has certainly succeeded, the one whom Allah has purified, so that it is thoroughly cleansed of disbelief and sins, and made right by righteous deeds.

The people of ta'wil (the interpreters, ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾: he says, "He has certainly succeeded who Allah has purified."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah, regarding ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾: they said, "Who makes it righteous."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he did not mention Ikrimah.
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾: "Whoever does good purifies it through obedience to Allah."
- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾: he said, "He has certainly succeeded who purifies his soul by righteous deeds."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾: he says, "He has certainly succeeded who Allah has purified."

This is the place of the oath (qasam), as:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: "The oath has occurred here, ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾." The readers (al-qurra') differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Hijaz and Syria recited ﴿fa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha﴾ with the fa', and so it is in their codices (masahif). The majority of the readers of Iraq in both cities recited it with the waw: ﴿wa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha﴾, and so it is in their codices.

The correct view on this is that they are two well-known recitations, not differing in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct.

The readers differed regarding the imalah (vowel inclination toward i) of words whose root letter is waw, in this surah and others, such as His saying ﴿and the moon when it follows it﴾ [91:2] and ﴿and by Him who spread it out﴾ [91:6], and similar. The majority of the readers of Kufa pronounced all of these with a fath (open vowel), while they inclined those whose root is ya'. Except 'Asim and al-Kisa'i: 'Asim pronounced all of these with fath, whether their root is waw or ya', without any inclination. Al-Kisa'i used kasr (a vowel closer to i) for all of them. Abu Amr looked at the consistency of the verse endings: if they are consistent in one vowel, he inclined all of them. As for the majority of the readers of Medina, they did not incline any of that to a strong imalah, nor did they open it to a strong fath, but took a middle course. The most eloquent and best of this is to look at the beginning of the surah: if its verse endings are in ya', all of them are recited with moderate (non-excessive) imalah; if its verse endings are in waw, they are recited with moderate fath, and all of them proceed with non-excessive fath. When one type occurs alone in a place, those with ya' are inclined with moderate imalah, and those with waw are opened with intermediate fath. If these were inclined and those were opened, it would not be a mistake, though the eloquent speech is that which we have described.

The readers (al-qurra') differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Hijaz and Syria recited ﴿fa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha﴾ with the fa', and so it is in their codices (masahif). The majority of the readers of Iraq in both cities recited it with the waw: ﴿wa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha﴾, and so it is in their codices.

The correct view on this is that they are two well-known recitations, not differing in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct.

The readers differed regarding the imalah (vowel inclination toward i) of words whose root letter is waw, in this surah and others, such as His saying ﴿and the moon when it follows it﴾ [91:2] and ﴿and by Him who spread it out﴾ [91:6], and similar. The majority of the readers of Kufa pronounced all of these with a fath (open vowel), while they inclined those whose root is ya'. Except 'Asim and al-Kisa'i: 'Asim pronounced all of these with fath, whether their root is waw or ya', without any inclination. Al-Kisa'i used kasr (a vowel closer to i) for all of them. Abu Amr looked at the consistency of the verse endings: if they are consistent in one vowel, he inclined all of them. As for the majority of the readers of Medina, they did not incline any of that to a strong imalah, nor did they open it to a strong fath, but took a middle course. The most eloquent and best of this is to look at the beginning of the surah: if its verse endings are in ya', all of them are recited with moderate (non-excessive) imalah; if its verse endings are in waw, they are recited with moderate fath, and all of them proceed with non-excessive fath. When one type occurs alone in a place, those with ya' are inclined with moderate imalah, and those with waw are opened with intermediate fath. If these were inclined and those were opened, it would not be a mistake, though the eloquent speech is that which we have described.

He, may He be exalted, says: And he has failed in his pursuit, and did not attain what he sought and aspired to for his own soul of righteousness, the one who corrupts it, meaning: the one whom Allah has corrupted (dassasa), who has made it obscure and debased it, by abandoning it to guidance, until he commits sins and abandons obedience to Allah. It was also said: dassaha (he corrupted it) is in fact dassasaha, and one of its sin letters (sin) was changed to a ya', as al-Ajjaj said:

*"The swooping of the falcon, when the falcon stoops"* [[I do not know the attribution of this line. I fear it is from verses which Daqqat al-Asadi says to Ma'n ibn Za'idah. Amali al-Murtada 1: 160.]]

He means taqaddud (the swooping). And "tazannaytu hadha al-amr" means "I suspected this matter," meaning tazannantu. The Arabs do this often: they change some letters of a doubled consonant, sometimes into ya' and sometimes into waw. From it is the saying of another:

*"It carries me in poetry through every art, until the tazannī turns me back from it."* [[Attributed by al-Mufaddal ibn Salamah in al-Fakhir: 253, who said: "The first to say that was Tarafah ibn al-Abd, in a poem in which he apologizes to Amr ibn Hind." It is not in his diwan. See Amthal al-Maydani 2: 125.]]

He means at-tazannun (the suspicion).

The people of ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾: he says, "And he has failed who Allah has corrupted and led astray."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾, meaning: its denial (of truth).
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾: one of them said, "He misled it," and the other said, "He led it astray."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾: he said, "He led it astray." And Sa'id said, "Who misled it."
- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words ﴿who corrupts it﴾: he said, "He misled it."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾: he said, "He sinned against it and committed immorality."
- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And he has failed﴾: he says, "And he has failed who Allah has corrupted (dassa) his soul."

**On the words of Allah, ﴿Thamud denied through its rebellion﴾ (91:11)**

He says: Thamud denied through their rebellion (tughwa), meaning: through the punishment which Salih (peace be upon him) promised them, and that punishment was a rebellious (ta'iyah) one which overwhelmed them, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming (al-ta'iyah)﴾ [69:5].

The people of ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this, although there is disagreement among the people of ta'wil.

Those who said what we have said about this:

- Sa'id ibn Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Salamah al-Filastini narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Samurah al-Madhhaji narrated to me, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿Thamud denied through its rebellion﴾: he said, "The name of the punishment which came to them was al-Taghwa, so he said: Thamud denied its punishment."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Thamud denied through its rebellion﴾: that is, the rebellion (al-tughyan).

Others said: Thamud denied through their disobedience to Allah.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿Thamud denied through its rebellion﴾: he said, "Its disobedience."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Thamud denied through its rebellion﴾: he said, "Through their transgression and their disobedience."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is through all of it together.

Those who said this:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub and Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Muhammad ibn Rifa'ah al-Qurazi, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, that he said: ﴿Thamud denied through its rebellion﴾: "Through all of it."
- Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed me, saying: Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Rifa'ah al-Qurazi, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, the same.

It was also said: ﴿Tughwaha﴾ means "their rebellion," and both are verbal nouns (masdar), for the sake of harmonizing the ends of the verses (ru'us al-ayy), since al-Tughwa is more similar to the other verse endings in this surah. This is like His saying ﴿and the last of their supplication (da'wahum)﴾ [10:10], meaning "the last of their supplication (du'a')."

**On the words of Allah, ﴿When the most wretched of them rose up﴾ (91:12)**

He says: When the most wretched of Thamud rose up, and he was Qudar ibn Salif.

As:

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: al-Tufawi narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Zam'ah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave a sermon, and mentioned in his sermon the she-camel and the one who hamstrung her, and said: "﴿When the most wretched of them rose up﴾ — a mighty, violent, unyielding man rose up for her among his kinsmen, like Abu Zam'ah."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, both saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿When the most wretched of them rose up﴾: meaning Uhaymar of Thamud.

**On the words of Allah, ﴿Then the Messenger of Allah said to them﴾ (91:13)**

By this He, may His praise be exalted, means: Salih, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), [meaning Salih, peace be upon him] said to the people of Thamud: ﴿The she-camel of Allah, and her drinking﴾: beware of the she-camel of Allah and her drinking. He only warned them about the drinking of the she-camel because he had previously informed them, by the command of Allah, that the she-camel had a turn to drink on one day, and they had a turn to drink on another day, other than the day of the she-camel, as I have already explained earlier.

And as:

- Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Then the Messenger of Allah said to them: The she-camel of Allah and her drinking﴾: the share (qism) of Allah which He allotted to her from this water.

**On the words of Allah, ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her﴾ (91:14)**

He says: They denied Salih regarding his report which he informed them of: that Allah, who made the she-camel's drinking a day, and their drinking a known day, and that Allah would bring down His vengeance upon them if they hamstrung her. As He, may His praise be exalted, described them, saying: ﴿Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity﴾ [69:4]. It is possible that the denial was through the hamstringing. When that is so, it is permissible to place the denial before the hamstringing, and the hamstringing before the denial, because every act which occurs as a result of a cause is good to begin with, either before the cause or after it, like the speaker's saying: "I gave and I did well," or "I did well and I gave," since giving is doing good, and doing good includes giving. Likewise, if the hamstringing was the cause of the denial, it is permissible for the speaker to put whichever of the two he wishes first.

Some have claimed that His saying ﴿But they denied him﴾ is a complete sentence in itself, and that His saying ﴿and hamstrung her﴾ is the answer (jawab) to His saying ﴿When the most wretched of them rose up﴾, as if it were said: "When the most wretched of them rose up and hamstrung her." It was asked: How is it said ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her﴾ when the people had, before the she-camel was killed, accepted that she had a day to drink and they had another day to drink? It was answered: The report has come that after their acceptance of that, they unanimously agreed to prevent her from drinking, and were content with her killing. By the consent of all of them her killer killed her, and whoever hamstrung her did so; for this reason the denial and the hamstringing were attributed to all of them. So He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her﴾.

**On the words of Allah, ﴿So He destroyed them, for their sin, and leveled them﴾ (91:14)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So their Lord crushed them (damdama) for their sin, that is, for that sin, their disbelief in Him, their denial of His messenger Salih, and their hamstringing of His she-camel. ﴿And leveled them﴾: He says, He leveled the destruction over all of them, so that not one of them escaped.

As:

- Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So their Lord crushed them for their sin, and leveled them﴾: it was reported to us that Uhaymar of Thamud refused to hamstring her until their young and their old, their males and their females, swore allegiance to him. When the people shared in hamstringing her, Allah crushed them for their sin and leveled them.
- Bishr ibn Adam narrated to me, saying: Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: When they hamstrung the she-camel, they sought her young one, and it went into a cleft of the mountain, so Allah cut off their hearts.

**On the words of Allah, ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾ (91:15)**

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: Its meaning is: He does not fear the consequence of His crushing them.

Those who said this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾: he said, "He does not fear any retribution from anyone (Allah)."
- Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamir narrated to me, saying: Uthman ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Murthid narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾: he said, "That is our Lord, blessed and exalted, who does not fear any retribution for what He did to them."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Amr ibn Munabbih, thus it is in my book, I heard al-Hasan recite ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾, and he said: "That Lord did that to them, and did not fear any retribution."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾: he said, "He does not fear their retribution."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾: he says, "He does not fear being pursued for anything He did to them."
- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾: Muhammad ibn Amr said in his report, "Allah said: ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾." Al-Harith said in his report: "Allah does not fear its consequence."
- Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Razin ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Abu Sulayman, who said: I heard Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani say regarding His words ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾: "Allah does not fear retribution."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: The one who hamstrung her did not fear its consequence, that is, the consequence (uqba) of his act which he did.

Those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Abu Rawq narrated to us, saying: al-Dahhak narrated to us, regarding ﴿And he does not fear its consequence﴾: "The one who hamstrung her did not fear its consequence."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And he does not fear its consequence﴾: "The one who hamstrung her did not fear its consequence."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And he does not fear its consequence﴾: "The one who does not fear what he did: the consequence of what he did."

The readers (al-qurra') differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Hijaz and Syria recited ﴿fa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha﴾ with the fa', and so it is in their codices (masahif). The majority of the readers of Iraq in both cities recited it with the waw: ﴿wa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha﴾, and so it is in their codices.

The correct view on this is that they are two well-known recitations, not differing in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct.

The readers differed regarding the imalah (vowel inclination toward i) of words whose root letter is waw, in this surah and others, such as His saying ﴿and the moon when it follows it﴾ [91:2] and ﴿and by Him who spread it out﴾ [91:6], and similar. The majority of the readers of Kufa pronounced all of these with a fath (open vowel), while they inclined those whose root is ya'. Except 'Asim and al-Kisa'i: 'Asim pronounced all of these with fath, whether their root is waw or ya', without any inclination. Al-Kisa'i used kasr (a vowel closer to i) for all of them. Abu Amr looked at the consistency of the verse endings: if they are consistent in one vowel, he inclined all of them. As for the majority of the readers of Medina, they did not incline any of that to a strong imalah, nor did they open it to a strong fath, but took a middle course. The most eloquent and best of this is to look at the beginning of the surah: if its verse endings are in ya', all of them are recited with moderate (non-excessive) imalah; if its verse endings are in waw, they are recited with moderate fath, and all of them proceed with non-excessive fath. When one type occurs alone in a place, those with ya' are inclined with moderate imalah, and those with waw are opened with intermediate fath. If these were inclined and those were opened, it would not be a mistake, though the eloquent speech is that which we have described.

**End of the tafsir of Surah al-Shams (Wa al-Shams wa Duhaha).**
